tier_reason: The python-xlsxio README table (script benchmark/benchmark.py, generator benchmark/generate_xlsx.py) shows the xlsxio-backed reader at 1.08584 s versus openpyxl read_only at 6.34512 s on a 100,000-row file, but gives only a kernel string: no CPU model, compiler, flags, Python or library versions. It is the wrapper author's own promotional table (9-star repo), not a well-known independent suite, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Big file (100,000 rows incl. header, 8 mixed-type columns), min of 3 runs: xlsxio with types 1.08584 s, without types 0.93787 s, without types all bytes 0.88268 s, with types from memory 1.09569 s, versus openpyxl read_only 6.34512 s, xlrd 4.10823 s, sxl 4.9788 s. Small file (100 rows): xlsxio with types 0.00128 s versus openpyxl 0.01131 s, xlrd 0.00486 s, sxl 0.00627 s. About 5.8x faster than openpyxl and 3.8x faster than xlrd on the big file with types (derived from page data); about 7.2x versus openpyxl with untyped bytes (derived from page data). The README's 'xlsx2csv' rows (6.53466 s big file) are not xlsx2csv: benchmark.py passes READ_OPENPYXL_SETUP/READ_OPENPYXL_STRING to all four xlsx2csv bench() calls, so they are a second openpyxl run and give no xlsx2csv comparison.
corrections.baseline: openpyxl (read_only=True, list(ws.iter_rows())); also xlrd (a pre-2.0 release, since xlrd 2.0 dropped .xlsx) and sxl in the same table. The table's xlsx2csv rows actually time openpyxl (copy-paste bug in benchmark.py), so xlsx2csv was never measured.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: not stated; setup.py builds the vendored xlsxio, expat, zlib and minizip C sources into one setuptools/Cython Extension with Python's default CFLAGS and the macros USE_MINIZIP, NOCRYPT, NOUNCRYPT (README says building from source with Cython gives about 5% more speed than the PyPI wheel); Python, Cython, openpyxl, xlrd and sxl versions not stated
corrections.caveats: Evidence is not from xlsxio's own repo (xlsxio's README and Changelog carry no performance numbers): the numbers measure the third-party python-xlsxio Cython wrapper (author Artur Beltsov, not the xlsxio author; last commit 2022-01-23, last PyPI release 0.1.5 on 2022-01-23), including Python object construction, against pure-Python libraries, so it shows C-versus-Python reading, not a C or C++ rival such as OpenXLSX or libxlsxwriter. The table dates from about June 2020 (kernel 5.4.44 built 2020-06-03, first PyPI release 2020-06-21) and used whatever xlsxio commit the wrapper vendored then (the submodule now points at b3dfd27). Harness flaws: the four 'xlsx2csv' rows run the openpyxl code (READ_OPENPYXL_* constants passed by mistake), so the xlsx2csv figures are a mislabelled second openpyxl run; generate_xlsx.py writes benchmark.xlsx (header plus 99,999 rows) while benchmark.py reads benchmark_big.xlsx and benchmark_small.xlsx, and the 100-row file is not scripted; the xlrd rows need xlrd below 2.0, which no longer reads .xlsx; openpyxl builds ReadOnlyCell objects while xlsxio returns plain values, and xlsxio needs column types supplied up front (or reads everything as str/bytes), so the work is not equal. Compiler flags, CPU model, Python version and library versions are not stated, so tier C. xlsxio fixed an integer underflow in minizip_io_memory_read_file_fn on 2026-09-24 (#150, the xlsxioread_open_memory path the wrapper's 'from memory' rows use) and a minizip reentry issue in xlsxio_read.c on 2026-06-28 (#148). No numeric comparison was found for the xlsxio writer or against another C/C++ xlsx reader. Ratios are computed from table rows, not quoted by the wrapper.

notes: Confirm at C: openpyxl, xlrd and sxl rows are genuine and the record's numbers match the README table, but the record also cited the xlsx2csv row, which benchmark.py actually fills with a second openpyxl run (copy-paste bug); claimed_speedup and baseline were corrected to drop it. Shortcomings to record: third-party 9-star wrapper benchmark from 2020, C versus pure-Python only (no C/C++ rival), no CPU/compiler/versions, mislabelled xlsx2csv rows, unequal work (cell objects vs plain values), xlrd row needs xlrd<2.0. Metadata checked: MIT, 525 stars, 131 forks, not a fork, not archived, last commit 2026-09-24.
